speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: On 26 January, I was deeply saddened when I was informed that Benjamin Lim, a student from North View Secondary School had passed away.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This passing of a young life is a tragic affair.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We cannot even begin to imagine what a difficult and painful time this must be for Benjamin's family, friends and schoolmates.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We extend to them our deepest and sincerest condolences.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Such public concerns and good intentions are fully understandable.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: However, I have chosen not to publicly respond earlier for the same reasons as the Minister for Home Affairs and Law.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I will do so now as the role played by our schools in the Police investigations has become a matter of public interest.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Such arrests involve theft, mischief by fire, wilful trespass, sexual offences, rioting and, in some cases, endangerment to life.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our schools have been working closely with the Police so that such behaviour can be curbed effectively and to ensure that these students are able to be guided back onto the right track through early education, intervention and reform.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Schools will always treat the interests and well-being of their students as a key priority.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Some members of the public have suggested that the schools' duty of care extends to shielding students from the Police and not releasing them to the Police without their parents' consent.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This sounds plausible, but it is not so straightforward.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Police carry out an important public function to uphold the law and keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: It is reasonable, and indeed expected, that our schools cooperate with Police investigations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In discharging their functions, the Police will decide if the interview with a student suspected of committing a crime or an offence should be conducted in school or at the Police Station.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our schools provide a safe, nurturing and conducive environment for learning.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our schools will always take appropriate steps to look after their students' interests and well-being, but they cannot do so in a manner that will obstruct the Police in their investigations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The following steps are carefully taken and consciously carried out when a student is asked to assist the Police in their investigations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: First, the teacher or staff will be discreet when bringing the student to meet with the Police.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: They will ensure that no undue attention is drawn to the student.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Second, the school leaders will first ascertain the student's physical and emotional well-being before letting the Police speak to the student.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The school leaders will also request that the number of Police officers speaking to the student be kept to a minimum.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Third, to afford greater assurance to the student, the school leaders or staff will request to be present if an initial interview is to be conducted at the school.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Fourth, should the Police decide to bring the student to the Police station for further questioning, the school will request that the Police first contact one of the student's parents to inform them of the situation and where the student will be brought to.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The school will also ensure that the student has something to eat or is not hungry.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Sixth, after the student is released by the Police, school staff will keep in touch with the parents of the student to render support and work out any follow-up steps to look after the well-being of the student.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Seventh, when the student returns to school, the school will closely monitor the well-being of the student.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Lastly, the school will protect the confidentiality of the student's identity and the on-going Police investigations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: These eight steps are not new to our schools.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In particular, when the Police first arrived and requested to speak with the student, the Principal sent a member of his staff to the canteen to look for Benjamin.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This was done discreetly and Benjamin was quietly brought to the Principal's office.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Principal spoke with Benjamin and informed him that a Police officer would be speaking with him.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Principal also assured Benjamin that he and his staff would stay with him throughout the meeting.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Thereafter, one Police officer entered the room to speak to Benjamin.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: At the end of the meeting, when Benjamin was required to go to the Police station, the Principal told Benjamin to call his mother.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Principal also ensured that Benjamin's mother knew where Benjamin would be taken to.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Principal also gave instructions to the school counsellor to give Benjamin's mother a call on the same day to check on Benjamin's well-being.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: At this juncture, Mdm Speaker, let me respond to two concerns raised by members of the public.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Post-questioning, the student will be released back to the direct care of his or her parents.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Nevertheless, the school's care for its student does not stop here.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: As I have mentioned, the school staff will get in touch with the student's parents to render support and work out any follow-up steps to look after the student's well-being.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The camp would have required Benjamin to be away from home for three days.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: His mother agreed and, hence, it was decided that Benjamin would stay at home.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Throughout the conversation, the school's motivation was to care for Benjamin's well-being.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our students are at the centre of their purpose and mission.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I know that they hold this commitment close to their hearts and discharge their responsibilities every day with professionalism.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In this, I stand fully behind my Principals, teachers and school staff.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I have, thus far, focused on what our schools do when the Police come to investigate one of their students.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This is only part of the overall picture.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: To steer our students away from crime, the Police and schools collaborate on various programmes and activities to educate students on the law, as well as to let them understand the consequences of crime, and help students who need specific Police support and intervention to extricate themselves from illegal activities or groups.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: There are also regular engagement sessions between the Police and school leaders and discipline masters.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: These sessions provide both sides the opportunities to clarify related issues, including those pertaining to Police Protocols.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Through these closer ground collaborations, the Police and our schools work towards a holistic solution to educate, prevent and address the issue of youth delinquency.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Coming back to Benjamin's case, I would like to mention one additional point.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The death of any single student has an immense impact on the entire school community.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: When news of Benjamin's death reached the school on the evening of 26 January, the school leaders and staff were shocked and distraught.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: There was absolutely no way that they could have foreseen what would happen.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The following day, the school leaders and staff attended Benjamin's wake.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Knowing how much Benjamin cherished and treasured his co-curricular activities with the National Police Cadet Corps (NPCC), the school arranged for his NPCC friends to write notes of condolences and fond memories of him to share with Benjamin's family.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Just as Benjamin's passing is mourned by his family, the school community and many others are also mourning.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Teachers and counsellors will continue to provide support to Benjamin's classmates and friends.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Whilst I know that nothing that I say today will bring Benjamin back, it is of utmost importance that we all learn from this tragedy.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We must always, always do our very best to reach out to those who may require attention and do whatever possible to prevent such terrible incidents from happening.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Once again, my colleagues and I would like to express our sincere condolences to Benjamin's family, friends and schoolmates.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Lastly, Mdm Speaker, I would like to share with the House that MOE is also participating in the Police review mentioned by the Minister for Home Affairs and Law.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: We have a bit of time for clarification.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Please raise your clarifications for the Minister for Home Affairs first, and then for the Minister for Education.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Can the Minister elaborate on the impact of youth crime on public safety and the challenges in dealing with youth crimes?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Although not common, we have had murder; we have had physical assault; we have had young people being picked up for gang riotings.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have young people involved in unlicensed moneylending activities, particularly arson.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think almost all Members would have come across that and how your residents fear for their safety.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, it presents a wide range of challenges.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is the fundamental Police approach − not criminalise, move them on to a crime-free life but, at the same time, when the incident happens, we have to move.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: A few years ago, we had a case of a 13-year-old boy raping his domestic helper.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Was the Police of the view that the offence, as founded upon the facts that the Minister has set out, was sufficiently grave and urgent that it could not and did not schedule for a later interview with the boy and his parents?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But I have gone into this in my Statement and suggested that we approach it with the facts known to the Police at that point in time.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When they went down to the school on 26 January, they did not know who the boy was.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They did not know what his antecedents were.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Some may have been reported; some may not have been reported.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If he had committed another molest, Members would be asking me, "Why did you not go down faster?" As a matter of principle, I think all Members will agree with me that when an offence has been committed, you want the Police to move as quickly as possible.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But we have the right Protocol on how a visit to a school should be handled.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There is a Protocol worked out with MOE.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, as little possibility of publicity as possible.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Unless as a society, we say that regardless of what happens, we should never go to the school.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I do not think Members will think that is a right approach.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My question or clarification is in relation to the Police Protocol: was there a need for five officers to go down to the school?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I appreciate that three of the five were from the NPC, but was there a need for three NPC officers?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I asked this clarification because I believe that the fundamental rationale for intervention where a youth offender is concerned is rehabilitation, to rehabilitate the youth.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And importantly, in order to rehabilitate, one has to rehabilitate in his or her own peer group.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For that purpose, it was the school or one of the peer groups was the school.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, was there a need to come to school in such numbers, and in order then for him to return to school to give him the best chance at rehabilitation?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, it is a question on Protocol and it is a question on Protocol going forward.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think the question is not so much focused on why five.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Because I agree with Mr de Souza that the focus should be on rehabilitation and the impact on the boy.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Therefore, you focus on how many spoke with him.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The three officers who went down from NPC were the bridges between the Police and the school.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When they go down, the school is familiar with these officers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They are able to know who to go to, who to speak with.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There are regular interactions between the NPC and that school, not just that school, but schools in the neighbourhood and the communities.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They open the doors, they speak with the Principals, they speak with the teachers and they say, "This matter needs to be investigated, our officers from division are here".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They were not present when the boy was interviewed.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In fact, only one of the officers from the division was present.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They went in unmarked cars in plain clothes.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, let us focus on what happened with the boy.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am not saying that one is always the right number.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think the point is, he must be interviewed in a way that is conducive for a fair, neutral approach to obtain the facts and to obtain the truth.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think that must be the fundamental aim.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: How you approach it is something that ground officers should be given the discretion to decide on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am not going to go into it and say, "It should have been five or it should have been three or it should have been four".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think those are ground decisions that we should leave to the officers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But we should look at it and we will certainly look at this case.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He saw one officer at first and then three brought him back, one left the car so there were only two which is the minimum number that you will need in a car.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And then he was interviewed by one officer in the division.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One of them both Ministers can jointly answer.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The first question is, will the Minister set the time frame or give a rough estimation as to when the Ministry hopes the reviews regarding the interview and handling of minors in Police custody will likely be completed.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second question is addressed to both Ministries; or both Ministers can jointly consider answering this: let us say in a scenario where the Principal or the Police has already informed the parent of a pupil who is under investigation that the Police have come to the school, will MOE or indeed MHA consider allowing a suitable member of the staff to accompany the pupil, the minor, to the Police station until at least the parents turn up, or until the pupil is released from the Police station?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am not talking about the situation where the pupil is under interview, not at that stage.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But what I am talking about is basically a member of the staff or allowing the parents to be at the Police Station but not during the interview so that, at the very least, there is some handing over between the school and the parents.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I do not really want to start consulting stakeholders before the Coroner's Inquiry.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, we will review it and that will really cover the Member's second point because in a sense, the Member's point is, can there be an adult accompanying the young person from school until he gets to the Police station?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think we will have to review those as part and parcel of this process.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have said earlier in my Statement that we will consider the suggestion of the Appropriate Adult scheme but I also pointed out the many considerations and why it is not so straightforward and some of the people involved would not be considered vulnerable either.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I gave you a range of cases and I gave you three major reasons why one should take a pause before rushing to conclusions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I want to assure Members and Mr Tan on one thing.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The reason why I gave you the statistics about 70% flowing through as it were without a charge, some of them after investigations are not guilty, but some of them would, in Police's view be people who have committed an offence.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But why is it that seven out of 10 are not charged?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is, therefore, not a Police versus a young person situation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Police look at it as a stakeholder in a community to try and make sure the young person gets rehabilitated.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That means you have really moved the young person from one path to another path.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As Mr Tan would know from practice, many of those who turn up in prison in their early 20s would often have had minor infractions in their teens.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The experience of criminality is a very strong indicator of subsequent life of crime.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, for us, the way we want to approach it is, lives saved.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have given you the facts that we have got to consider, but that does not mean that we sit back and say we do nothing.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will review and we will consider the point.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Losing a child is every parent's worst nightmare and every parent wants their sons and daughters to be safe.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Yesterday, website 	The Online Citizen	 (TOC) quoted Benjamin's father as saying, "If not for social media, especially TOC, the case would have died down a long time ago." But the Minister said that Benjamin's father wanted to be out of the spotlight.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can the Minister help explain why the TOC article paints such a different picture of Benjamin's father?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: First of all, the suggestion that this case would have died down long ago is ridiculous because there is going to be a Coroner's Inquiry.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is what normally happens when there is an unnatural death and an announcement was made on the 1 February, as I said, that is six days after the Police started investigating; on the sixth day.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But I am not saying that the father is saying absurd things; I do not want to assume that what I see in TOC is what the father says.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What I can say is what the father said to us.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They would appreciate if Police could inform the media not to publish the family's pictures or names, and I elaborated upon that in my Statement.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Mr Lim, the father, confirmed that yesterday with the Police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That was yesterday, the same day the Member referred to this article coming out.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Many possible explanations; I have not sought to ask why.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Is it the case that the father is saying different things to different people?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Or is it the case that, as usual, you cannot believe what you read on TOC?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I also thank the Ministers for taking this case seriously to issue the Statements.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: My question is about the Appropriate Adult scheme.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Currently, it covers persons with mental and intellectual disability only.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In regimes like in the United Kingdom, the scope covers young people who are less than 18 years of age and also vulnerable adults who might have mental wellness issues or even dementia or other learning disabilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister to consider this.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The second question is: the current Appropriate Adult scheme in Singapore is manned by volunteers and run by charities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I think the scheme is important enough for the state to allocate some resources to ensure that at least people who are trained, not just trained for a short while only, people who are professionals, can operate the scheme on a sustainable basis.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I assume on the second question, what the Member is really asking is whether we will pay for it.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I cannot give a guarantee on that but we will certainly look at.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But I have taken some considerable pains to point out why it is not a straightforward issue and what are possible issues that might arise.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have to balance between the need to move quickly, investigate, particularly when it is a serious crime, a terrorism-related issue, and balance that against the need for the young person to have some support.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have mentioned the systemic risk could be minimised as well.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will try but I just want to be very open, clear and transparent about our considerations as we look at this.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can the Minister elaborate on his assessment of TOC's motivations, conduct and coverage of this tragic event?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is quite clear from my Statement what I thought of the coverage.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think it is a calculated, cynical attempt to tar the Police using falsehoods.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And I have said what should happen hereafter is not something I should be commenting on today.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For the Minister for Home Affairs, I understand the urgency the Police had in interviewing the deceased, but could the Police not have waited another half an hour or one hour until Benjamin's father or mother came to the Police station or the school before starting to interview him?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Like what the Minister mentioned earlier, this is his first offence.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: He did not have any prior record, and as a 14-year-old whom I still regard as a child, he must have felt quite frightened to be there being interviewed by the Police without a significant adult present.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The other question: there are many speculations, accusations and unverified accounts on social media sites.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In future, will the Ministry be more responsive and open to sharing more information in both print and online news media so as to make verifications or to dispel the accusations that are floating around?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think the first question essentially raises the question whether we should have an Appropriate Adult present.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What I have said is we had considered a lot of that very carefully previously and I have explained in my Statement the considerations.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And I have said that we will review.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will look at the findings in the Coroner's Inquiry.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will consult stakeholders and we will decide.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have explained why we should not have knee-jerk reactions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think I should express, as the Minister for Education has expressed, our condolences to Benjamin's family.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And equally, we share the grief of the family of the 11-year-old girl because they are also grief-stricken.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think they all have the same feelings.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As I said in my Statement, either child could have been a child of any of us.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We got to approach it with that perspective.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: At the same time, whether the Police should wait for the parents or somebody else to accompany, whether there should be someone else present, I think these are the same type of questions that Ms Denise Phua and Mr Dennis Tan have raised and which I myself have raised in my Statement.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the second point as to whether we will release more information, I have spent quite a bit of time explaining why in this case we actually decided not to go into the facts.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think it would be unseemly for this matter to get to a stage where there are series of allegations and counter allegations, and statements and counter statements with the families, the commentators, the Police – you will have a "free for all".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is precisely what legal proceedings are destined to avoid.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will have a proper process for finding out the facts.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Otherwise, who is to say my truth is superior to your truth?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think we were right, we were observing the law but others were not so careful.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In fact, they were cavalier and which has then required us to come out today and clarify.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: On the same track as what Member Intan has asked with regard to online reports, I think we cannot ignore the fact that the online media play a very important part in communication.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In situations like that where it is very emotive and sensitive, while I totally understand the stance of handling the information very carefully and the sensitivity of sharing the information, is there a way that information, at least some information can be shared with online news sites in a way that would help, at least, not continue to fire these emotions in respect of the families?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I know it is a very hard balance.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The other thing is also, should online websites obtain and verify information of this nature before they post such articles?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is not for them to make the allegations and then for us to respond.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, we start with what is the law.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As I said, you can raise some general issues; you can raise the issue of policy, whether in the media, physical media, print media, broadcast media or online media.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is even egregious when they are a bunch of lies.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think the starting point is people who want to express their views have to be responsible and the law requires them to be responsible.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will be as open as is legally possible.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Where it is possible, we will publish the information.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The mere presence of an MOE staff at the Police station before the parents arrive will give much assurance to the student while he is under Police custody.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It is currently premature to position one way or the other.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: If you look at the process of the school, they would ensure that the well-being of the student is first taken care of when the Police moves the child or student to the Police station.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: And in the process, there would be no further contact between the school staff and the student.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, in the process of movement, the Police will be with the student in the Police car.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: And when they reach the Police station, the Police will have the interview process away from any waiting room.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: At the end of the interview, when the parents are there, the handing over of the student will be to the direct care of the parents.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, the school staff essentially will have no contact with the student in the current Protocol.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In the review, we will be working with the Police to see what the review outcomes may be.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: A question for the Minister to let me understand the Protocol a bit better: at the moment, do the Principals of the schools have any discretion at all to decide whether or not to release their pupils for questioning by the Police in school or to the custody of the Police?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: If they do have such discretion, perhaps the Minister could share with us what are some of the guidelines for this discretion.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The second question is more of a suggestion for the current review: would the Ministry consider requiring the Principals to inform the parents of any pupil immediately upon the arrival of the Police at the school to interview the pupil or to take the pupil into custody, rather than to advise or inform the Police to inform the parents?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: When the Police invite or take someone for an interview, it is up to the Police to decide where and when the interview would take place.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But over time, the schools and the Police have worked together to ensure that the well-being of the students are taken care of.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: On the second part, each incident is unique and at what stage the Principal would get the student to call the parents will all be contextualised.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In this particular instance, where the interview was in a calm manner, the whole eight-step process could carry through as how I have articulated.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But in certain instances and context, you would understand that the real ground processes may be somewhat more flexible.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: And also, in answer to the Member's earlier question, the Minister for Home Affairs has pretty much answered most of it.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I would just like to emphasise that we are open to review and adapt our processes where needed to make sure that the students could be accompanied if the review conclusions allow us to do so.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My question is this: for MOE, how many times in the past three years has the same Protocol been applied in the schools?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Has MOE received any feedback or comments from parents with regard to this Protocol, where Police comes to the school to do investigations?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And thirdly, what measures are in place in schools to help students, I think "rehabilitation" is the key word used earlier, rehabilitate and integrate back into school life once investigations are over?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am sure in this era of social media, friends will talk and if it goes around, there will be other implications.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And, specifically, for this particular case, did the school interview friends?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I suppose in schools, cyber bullying is one aspect; other aspects are rumours and other things that go round in social media or on Whatsapp or social media platforms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Was there such evidence that this may have happened that led to his choice of actions?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: At this stage, we do not yet know the reasons for Benjamin's decision to end his life, whether it is social media or other factors> It is premature to make any conclusions.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, I will just leave it as that.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: These processes that we have adopted are practised and refined over this period of time.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: When the school takes the student back, the balance between confidentiality and rehabilitation is a very delicate one.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The counsellors, some are trained with the National Institute of Education (NIE) and some of them are even ex-teachers.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: They would be able to contextualise their approaches to counselling according to the needs of the students, depending on the severity of the case, how emotionally impacted the student may be.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: All these would be factors that the counsellors would have to take into consideration and make his or her judgement to tailor the counselling.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Has MOE received any feedback or comments from parents with regard to this Protocol for Police investigations on students?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In terms of feedback, I do not have the information with me.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I will share that feedback with you offline.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I will add that the young persons are especially vulnerable in terms of the stage of their mental development to suicide risk.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: If they do think that there are added risks, they will refer the student to psychiatric help or a psychologist's help outside the school, in the hospitals or in other clinics.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Was Benjamin taken for questioning by the Police during school hours?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: If so, from what I understand, during school hours, permission is required from the parents or legal guardian before students can leave the school.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: My second question is: should the school counsellor or a school staff member not have met Benjamin and the mother or the father in person to find out whether Benjamin would want to continue with the school camp, rather than doing that through a phone call?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I think the Minister for Home Affairs can confirm that.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I am not an expert in that area, but that is as far as I can understand.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: And I did not get the Member's second question.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: When the school counsellor or the school staff member called up Benjamin's mother to ask whether he wanted to continue with the school camp the following day, could it not have been better communicated; could they not have met in person?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We must move back to the incident without hindsight.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Of course, with hindsight of what has happened, we can always do better.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: These are the things that we can review.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But in terms of calling the parent to check on how Benjamin was doing, it is not an unreasonable thing to do.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It is a very tragic incident, no doubt, but at the moment, we really do not know what was the trigger for Benjamin.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: This may or may not imply that the school counsellors should be present during the interview.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: I will leave it to the Education Minister to answer the question.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: At the moment, I do not quite have the details.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Perhaps, in another occasion where a PQ is filed, I can get back to the Member on these specific details.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If not, will the current review process consider putting in place such a regime, whereby that kind of help can be given to young persons who are being investigated?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That can come about, perhaps, by way of the Ministry and the schools working with Voluntary Welfare Organisations (VWOs) or Non-governmental Organisations (NGOs) and so on?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: When the student comes back to the school, the counsellor and the teachers will get with the student and the parents to render support and work through what may be the needed steps.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Beyond the school, the counsellor also has networks with the Family Services Centres (FSCs).
